description: Every villager has a name, a face, hair and clothes of their own, built from the player model and vanilla gear.
Villagers are faintly see-through with a soft teal glow after dark, as echoes in Valheim's afterlife.
Each villager claims a bed, goes to sleep at his own bedtime and gets up at dawn; without a bed he rests under a roof.
With no work to do, villagers sit by the fire, take a bench, stroll, chat and keep busy at the stations.
Villagers cook real food at the hearth, keep meals in the chest, and the hurt eat to heal like a player does.
Each villager has a mood with reasons you can read (slept well, ate well, got hurt), and the village has a mood of its own.
A small camp is happy with little; a grown village wants a longhouse, seats, a fence and varied food.
Villagers who lack a bed, food or safety grumble, then ask you for help, and in the end pack up and move to a neighbour.
Couples with a home and a free bed have children, who grow up and take after their parents.
Long-lived villagers become elders who work lighter and tell old stories, and one day die in their sleep and are mourned.
Every villager has a friend and a rival; friends choose beds near each other and rivals keep apart.
Each villager has a homeland, a favourite food, a fear, a pastime and a hope, and they show in what he says and does.
The first settler still living leads the village, greets strangers first and speaks at gatherings.
Villagers walk around the village, run only on errands, open and close doors and keep out of fires.
notes: Walking jitter is still being fixed.

description: Everyone eats from the chest each day, and a hungry village works slower.
Huts, houses and halls each want more (food, then meat and mead, then bread and coal), and a full, content home gets upgraded.
Illness can spread, clean water from a well helps, and a healer tends the sick in bed.
notes: A one-off fever event is built.

description: Villagers need warm clothes or a fire in winter.
A villager at the end of his rope sulks or shouts at his rival for an hour, then calms down.
The village keeps a small shrine where villagers leave offerings and pray.

feature: Thousands of lines in eight voices
description: Villagers talk about their work, wants, the weather, the time of day, where they stand and what you carry, each in his own voice, without repeating himself.
Two or three villagers chat, and what they say depends on whether they are friends, rivals, sweethearts or workmates.
Your visits, gifts, kills, deaths and blows are remembered, and villagers who saw them tell the rest.
Villagers remark when the weather turns, at dawn and dusk, when a boss falls, when you draw a weapon or sneak, and when beasts come near.
Villagers glance at each other and at you, answer your waves, come to sit with you by the fire and bring a meal when you are hurt.
Each villager wants something for a few days (a bed, a feast, a hunt), friends court and become sweethearts, and rivals make peace.
Villagers remember yesterday, newcomers tell why they left home, and each village starts with a short history of its own.
notes: The founding history is an idea.

description: Idle villagers walk over to watch a neighbour work, comment on it, and pick up a little of the skill.
Each villager has a friendship with you that grows with talk and gifts he likes, with birthdays, letters and special scenes along the way.
inspired_by: Stardew Valley, Animal Crossing, MCA Reborn

description: Rude words can turn into a fist fight between two villagers while others gather to watch.
Big events slowly change a villager's character, and villagers approve or object to what you do.
Talking to a villager opens a short set of questions and answers that depend on your standing, quests and the time.
Children chase each other and play games round the village.
Villagers take what lies on the ground first, then felled logs, then fresh trees and rocks, pick the right tree for the wood they need, and stop when the village needs nothing.
A builder raises each building from the ground up, hammering every piece in place, and stops to fight when he has to.
Villagers are protectors or carers, and from six villagers on they take trades (carpenter, woodcutter, miner, cook, farmer), though anyone can do any job.
notes: Roles never depend on gender (Tyler).

description: Hunters bring meat, foragers pick berries and mushrooms, and farmers tend rows behind the farms.
notes: Crops from seeds are planned.

description: The smith makes each tier of tools, weapons and armour at the real station from the chest, and the village later builds its own forge.
Villagers get better at what they do, work faster with practice, and trades go to the most skilled.
A happy village builds and works a little faster, a glum one slower.
notes: Goes against your 2026-11-05 decision that mood changes free time only.

description: A carer tends the hearth each morning, idle villagers add benches and a cooking station, and a fire keeper keeps every fire and torch going.
notes: The fire keeper is an idea.

description: Villagers run the charcoal kiln, smelter, fermenter, mill and oven from the chest, keeping a set amount of each good.
A beekeeper keeps crafted bee hives and a brewer makes mead.
notes: Crafted hives are fine; wild hives stay out.

description: A villager fishes from the shore, a dock or a raft.
You see the builder carry each load of wood and stone from the chest to the site.
Ask a villager to gather or help on your own build for a while.
Now and then a villager is struck by inspiration, takes over a station and makes one fine item.
A worker who lacks a tool asks for it and a crafter makes it.
notes: Touches the one-chest rule.

description: Fields tire if the same crop grows too long, and blight or rats can hit the stores.
Villages build houses copied from the game's own locations and installed mods, clean and lived in.
Homes first, then a longhouse round the hearth, a hub with the notice board, a workshop and a storehouse, then more as it grows.
Buildings are rebuilt bigger and better, interiors fill out, and small decorations are added between upgrades.
A village only builds with what its biome gives, until its outposts bring other materials home.
Your chosen designs for each biome, each with structure and decor stages the village grows through.
Villages may also build designs the lab made, once you approve them.
notes: Needs the CLAUDE.md wording agreed.

description: The builder puts back broken pieces, and empty houses slowly fall into disrepair.
One chest by the hearth holds the materials that you and the villagers bring, and a notice board shows what the village needs.
The hearth grows from a campfire to a hearth with a cooking station and then larger fires.
A building can catch fire; rain or the villagers put it out, or it burns to a ruin that the builder rebuilds.
A room becomes a bedroom, kitchen or smithy by what is in it, and good rooms make people happier.
A village that likes you enough builds you a house.
Pick a design or a plot and the village builds it from its chest.
A big village builds one landmark of its own.
A see-through preview shows where the next building will stand.
Rare village sites are spread through the world, each founded with a name, settlers and a map pin when you first come near.
The longhouse sits at the centre, homes round it, workshops and farms further out, doors facing the hearth or the road.
Each village is a woodland, fortified or farming village and grows, guards and forages to match.

feature: A fence that becomes a wall
description: A light fence rings the village, turns into a stake wall, and later a stone wall as it grows.
Villages in different biomes build different houses and look different, with Fuling and Dvergr styles further on.
Villages are laid out round a plaza, along a street or at a crossroads, with plots on both sides of the road.
Homes grow a garden, woodpile, drying rack or pen behind them, some with a fence.
A well or a maypole green where roads meet and villagers gather.
Woodland villages keep trees between their houses.
Claim a village as yours or join one and help run it.
A villager walks each new path with a hoe; roads branch from the centre and busy stretches get wider.
Dirt trails link neighbouring villages and outposts, with signposts where they leave and meet.
Each building stands on flat ground at floor height, and villagers level the village spot by spot with soft edges.
notes: Spot-by-spot levelling is an idea.

description: Paths wear into the ground where villagers walk often and fade when unused.
Main streets go from dirt to gravel to stone or planks as the village grows.
Paths never get too steep, and small bridges and boardwalks cross gaps, streams and swamp.
Torches line the main street and lamp posts stand along the trails.
Villages can have real streams that run downhill, ponds and falls you can swim in.
Villages on the coast build docks and boathouses.
Roads between villages exist before anyone walks them.
Every felled tree is replanted outside the village, and villages short of trees plant groves.
Farms get tamed boars and piglets over time, then pens and chickens.
notes: Feeding animals goes against your rule that animals come on a schedule.

description: Villagers plant berry rows and groves they fell years later.
Forests regrow from seed and bushes return sooner near a forager.
Game thins out where it is hunted hard and comes back over time.
A few tamed wolves guard the village.
Plains villages keep lox in a pen.
Stone and ore veins slowly come back near quarries.
notes: Creates resources the game does not restore.

description: Crops grow in their seasons and fields rest in winter.
notes: Farms already rest in winter.

description: Buy from what the village can spare, at prices that depend on how it sees you.
notes: Off by default.

description: The village pays for materials you bring and asks you once a day for what it is short of.
Travelling pedlars trade with the village and sell you gear it cannot make.
The notice board posts paid work for what the village lacks.
The village's top need shows as a pile or item by the chest.
Villages send what they can spare to neighbours along the trails, with a pack animal and loads both ways.
notes: Return loads and the pack animal are planned.

description: One day a week the hub fills with pedlars, visitors and better prices.
Goods are cheap where caravans bring them and dear where they are short, and each village is known for one good.
A village that counts you a hero leaves you a basket of food, a share of its goods, or rent from houses you built.

feature: Banker, market and games of chance
description: Keep coins with a villager, sell to other players at the village, or try your luck.
inspired_by: Marketplace NPCs, Travs Valheim Server NPCs

description: Carry loads between villages to earn standing.
The village trader offers more after you bring him finds from dungeons.
Protectors take up arms, carers shelter indoors, and idle protectors watch the edge of the village.
One protector walks the edge each night with a torch.
Bigger villages draw raids at night, announced at dusk with a direction, growing with the village and easing after a bad loss.
notes: Out of scope; RaidsEnabled stays off.

description: Blow the horn at the hearth and the protectors follow you for a while, and they run out to help a friend in a fight.
A player the village dislikes is met by armed protectors, and a hated one may be hunted.
notes: Off by default since 2026-11-08 (Hostility setting).

description: Help beat a raid and the village cheers you and gives you better prices.
A village may raid a neighbour it hates and send help to one it likes.
Caravans can be ambushed on the trail.
Outlaw camps near a village grow if left alone and start to raid.
Hire a warrior, hunter or seeress who follows you, levels up and wears the gear you give.
Archers on watchtowers shoot raiders, and signal fires give earlier warning.
Protectors hold a shield wall, walk patrols, are tended by a healer and need feeding and pay.
Coastal villages face raiders who land by boat.
Raiders demand a toll; pay it or fight.
Strangers cannot break or build inside a village.
The sky turns red and a horde comes.
Villages like or dislike each other, and it changes day by day.
Visitors carry each village's news to the next, and villagers talk about it.
Pilgrims stay the night and leave a blessing; hermits by old ruins mark a place worth finding on your map.
A visitor who slept badly leaves sour, a happy one brings a gift and may ask to stay.
Each village's view of you rises and falls with what you do; below a point it wants a fine before it will trade.
Grown villages set up logging, flint, mining and fishing camps, once they have the gear to defend them, and haul the goods home.
notes: Mining and fishing camps are planned.

description: A full village sends settlers to found a new village nearby in its own style.
The board and the Jarl ask for help with real places on your map, with bounties, favours and lost villagers to find.
Strangers in the longhouse tell their story and would join for a price.
Protectors leave on journeys and come back days later with loot, or not at all.
Free a smith held at a camp and he joins a village with his trade.
Villagers walk the trail to see a friend in the next village and come back with news.
A village whose people all died or moved away is settled again by newcomers a few days later.
notes: EmptyVillageReturnDays (3).

description: Villagers scout the land, mark dungeons and pass on rumours of treasure.
Villages claim land, form alliances and can be taken over.
Pay a villager to walk you to a village you have found.
Once a year a great caravan comes from far away.
Marry a villager and have an heir.
Villages keep a calendar of seasons and days, and follow the Seasons mod when it is installed.
Sowing feast, midsummer fire, harvest feast and Yule: work stops early and the evening is a feast with visitors.
Villages store more in autumn, rest in winter and feel the cold when wood runs low.
A finished building, a newcomer, a birth or a felled boss brings the village together, and good days end with a feast and dancing.
Small good and bad days happen: a harvest, a visiting skald, a lost traveller, a fever, beasts at night, a quarrel.
A thief sneaks in at night and robs the chest.
Villagers head under a roof when it rains.
A dry spell slows the farms.
At Yule the village puts up the game's Yule pieces.
Weddings and funerals gather the village, and the dead get a cairn.
A village grows from camp to hamlet to village to town as it gains people and buildings.
How well a village is doing drives visitors, newcomers and raids, and drops after a death or a raid.
Each boss felled lets the villages grow one stage further.
Villagers' tools and weapons get better as the village grows.
Helping the village, its people and its knowledge unlock new buildings and bonuses.
You choose rules for the village that trade one benefit for another.
Villages save with the world and are shared by everyone on the server, with settings set by the host.
Every player's deeds count, everyone sees villagers sit and sleep, and dedicated servers run everything.
Parties count as one in a village's eyes, and a board ranks those who helped most.
Look at a villager to see what he is doing and why, and at the hearth for the village's summary and mood.
The hearth keeps the village's history of settlers, buildings, births, deaths and raids.
notes: A readable book is an idea.

description: The board shows the village's level, people, next project and needs.
Each village has a map pin that grows with it, and villagers show as dots inside it.
Windows show the village's people, needs and history, a villager's mood, skills and friends, and your quest journal.
Raids and fires come with a message and a pin on your map.
Pilgrims, seers or the Jarl can give you a short blessing.
Tell protectors where to stand or whom to follow.
In the evening villagers sit with their own pastime by the fire: carving, mending gear, telling a story, using the game's own animations.
Once the village has a hot tub, villagers soak in it after work and on cold nights.
When a child grows up, the village gathers round him, he takes up a trade and gets his own bed.
Children follow an elder or a tradesman about for a while and start out with some of his skill.
Villagers put on capes in rain and winter and take them off in summer.
Ask the smith or a crafter for an item, leave the materials in the chest, and it waits for you there once it is made.
Meals sit on tables, the cauldron simmers, and the stores show on shelves and item stands, so you can tell a well-fed village at a glance.
A herder walks the village's boars or lox out to graze by day and back to the pen at dusk.
The cook makes the game's own recipes at the cauldron and oven, and feast tables are set with the real dishes.
Invite villagers to keep your fires fed, your kilns filled and your fields picked while you are away.
Smiths and protectors keep weapons, shields and armour on the game's racks and armour stands.
The village picks a big shared goal (a bridge, a mill, a new hall), shows it on the board, and everyone, you included, chips in until a feast marks it done.
Grown villages by a river build a water wheel, and those on a windy hill a windmill, for their flour.
Trophies and rare finds you give the village are hung in the longhouse, with a line in the chronicle.
At dusk a villager lights the lanterns and braziers, and at bedtime the fires are banked.
The longhouse keeps a bed for you that you can sleep in and set as your spawn.
Each village takes its own colours and hangs its banners on the longhouse, gates and boats.
A raised stone near the village records the names of the dead and the village's great days.
On long trails villagers keep a lean-to with a campfire where travellers and you can rest.
Coastal villages sail a karve to fish and to visit other coastal villages.
Coastal villages keep a beacon lit at night to guide boats home.
Deer and birds come close to quiet villages and keep away from busy ones.
Friendly villages send guests to each other's festivals, and you can walk over with them.
Festivals have archery at targets, foot races and drinking contests that you can join.
After you fell a boss, the skald tells the tale at the next feast and the village keeps it in its saga.
Each village becomes known for what it makes most (mead, fish, ironwork), and pedlars carry it to others.
When a village reaches a new stage it holds a feast and gives you something from what it makes.
